definitions.explanation: The way or method of doing something. Often used with verbs to describe how something is done.

examples.japanese: この{機械|きかい}の{使|つか}い{方|かた}を{教|おし}えてください。
examples.english: Please teach me how to use this machine.
It can't be helped. / There's nothing that can be done.

examples.japanese: {食|た}べ{方|かた}が{分|わ}からない。
examples.english: I don't know how to eat this.

notes:
{仕方|しかた} means 'way of doing' and is often combined with verb stems.

COMMON PATTERN: [Verb stem] + {方|かた}
- {使|つか}い{方|かた}: way of using
- {読|よ}み{方|かた}: way of reading
- {書|か}き{方|かた}: way of writing
- {作|つく}り{方|かた}: way of making

KEY EXPRESSION:
{仕方|しかた}がない / {仕方|しかた}ない: It can't be helped, there's no way around it. This is one of the most important Japanese expressions, reflecting acceptance of situations beyond one's control.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {方法|ほうほう}: method (more formal)
- やり{方|かた}: way of doing (casual)
